campaign_note: Privilege-escalation link in a three-CVE Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain (with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527) used by a threat actor Volexity tracks as UTA0576; Ivanti describes exploitation as limited and no victim or compromised-appliance count has been published.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Volexity blog (chain exploited from 2026-10-03; Defused separately reported signs of CVE-2026-104935 exploitation from 2026-10-01, per BleepingComputer)

evidence.counts_what: Internet-exposed Ivanti Connect Secure instances (all versions; not a count of vulnerable or compromised devices; article says it is unknown how many are already secured)
evidence.measured_by: Shadowserver, as reported by BleepingComputer
evidence.quote: Shadowserver now tracks over 5,000 Internet-exposed ICS instances

evidence.counts_what: Ivanti Connect Secure instances exposed online at initial disclosure of the chain (not a count of vulnerable or compromised devices; may include honeypots)
evidence.measured_by: Shadowserver, as reported by BleepingComputer
evidence.quote: Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver now tracks over 5,500 ICS instances exposed online

evidence.counts_what: Volexity's report describes one compromised, fully patched ICS appliance at one of its monitoring customers; it is a case description, not a population count
evidence.measured_by: Volexity
evidence.quote: starting on October 3, 2026, UTA0576 repeatedly exploited these vulnerabilities to compromise the ICS VPN appliance

evidence.counts_what: Vendor characterization of exploitation scale at disclosure of the chain
evidence.measured_by: Ivanti, quoted by BleepingComputer
evidence.quote: At the time of disclosure, Ivanti is aware of limited exploitation in the wild.

campaign_note: File-upload/predictable-identifier link in the same UTA0576 Ivanti Connect Secure chain as CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-111357; the Volexity post as fetched names only the other two CVE IDs, so attribution of this CVE to the chain rests on CISA's KEV text and trade press.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Volexity blog, which says CVE-2026-104935 was chained 'with two other flaws' from 2026-10-03 (as relayed by BleepingComputer); this CVE ID itself first appears as exploited in the 2026-10-30 KEV addition and BleepingComputer 2026-11-02

evidence.counts_what: Internet-exposed Ivanti Connect Secure instances (all versions; not a count of vulnerable or compromised devices; article says it is unknown how many are already secured)
evidence.measured_by: Shadowserver, as reported by BleepingComputer
evidence.quote: Shadowserver now tracks over 5,000 Internet-exposed ICS instances

evidence.value: since at least October 1 (no count given)
evidence.counts_what: Duration of zero-day exploitation of the chain; no victim count
evidence.measured_by: BleepingComputer (citing Defused and Volexity)
evidence.quote: have been chained in zero-day attacks since at least October 1

campaign_note: 'Fragnesia' local privilege escalation (public PoC since 2026-05-13) reported by Dream Security as chained after the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618/-109619) to root 25 servers in four countries, three of them at a US government-affiliated organization; CISA did not confirm those details.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Dream Security report ('Monday report' per BleepingComputer, 2026-10-29); a Qualys ThreatPROTECT post dated 2026-05-15 carries 'Exploited in Attacks' in its headline but was not verified here

evidence.counts_what: Servers rooted via the PHP2Shell + Fragnesia chain, across the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea (campaign artifacts observed by Dream Security)
evidence.measured_by: Dream Security, as reported by BleepingComputer
evidence.quote: This included artifacts of a campaign that had rooted 25 servers across the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea.

evidence.counts_what: Servers the attacker focused on inside one US government-affiliated environment; subset of the 25
evidence.measured_by: Dream Security, as reported by BleepingComputer
evidence.quote: Once rooted, the attacker zeroed in on three specific servers in a US government-affiliated environment.

evidence.counts_what: Same campaign as reported by CSO Online; a Securonix commenter characterizes the victims as mostly firewall appliances
evidence.measured_by: Dream Security, as reported by CSO Online
evidence.quote: to breach 25 servers, including three affiliated with the US government.

campaign_note: Outlook spoofing flaw (NTLMv2 hash disclosure when a user opens a crafted message file) released 2026-11-10 and flagged 'Exploitation Detected' by Microsoft; no third-party reporting or scale figures were found.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Microsoft MSRC Security Update Guide (exploited: Yes; publicly disclosed: No)

evidence.counts_what: Vendor exploitability assessment; no victim, target or volume count
evidence.measured_by: Microsoft MSRC (read via the Security Update Guide API, https://api.msrc.microsoft.com/sug/v2.0/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2026-124194)
evidence.quote: Exploitation Detected

campaign_note: 'SSHole' password-authentication bypass affecting sshd on musl-libc systems without PAM (notably Alpine Linux), fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2 on 2026-11-05; Previdian honeypots recorded exploitation attempts within nine hours of CVE publication and one successful root login on a honeypot, with no real-world victim or exposure counts published.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Previdian (CEO Ryan Dewhurst), reported by Help Net Security and The Hacker News

evidence.counts_what: Exploitation attempts against Previdian honeypot sensors, all from one Japan-geolocated IP and one sensor
evidence.measured_by: Previdian, as reported by Help Net Security
evidence.quote: So far, the company has counted eight attempts, all from that single Japan-based address and all caught by one sensor.

evidence.counts_what: Updated count of exploitation attempts and source IPs (nine countries); the article update does not restate who measured it, earlier figures were Previdian telemetry
evidence.measured_by: The Hacker News update (presumably Previdian telemetry; measurer not named in the update)
evidence.quote: the number of exploitation attempts has increased to 20 and originated from 13 unique IP addresses

evidence.counts_what: Time from CVE publication to first observed exploitation attempt
evidence.measured_by: Previdian, as reported by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: observed the first exploitation attempt less than nine hours after the CVE publication

evidence.counts_what: Successful root access by an attacker on a Previdian honeypot running real Alpine Linux and OpenSSH
evidence.measured_by: Previdian, as reported by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: confirmed successful root access on a honeypot running Alpine Linux and OpenSSH

campaign_note: CVSS 4.3 file-type-restriction bypass in a carrier webmail component; JVN relays the developer's statement that attacks have been observed, while the vendor's own GitHub advisory says nothing about exploitation and no press or telemetry coverage was found.

first_exploitation_claim.source: JVN (JPCERT/CC and IPA) advisory JVNVU#93403064, relaying the developer

evidence.counts_what: Developer statement relayed by JVN that exploitation has been observed; no count of systems, organizations or attempts
evidence.measured_by: Openwave Messaging (developer), via JVN
evidence.quote: The developer states that attacks exploiting the vulnerability have been observed.

campaign_note: One of the two 'PHP2Shell' unauthenticated RCE flaws patched 2026-10-21; exploit attempts began before the patch and reached millions per Cloudflare, the first working in-the-wild RCE was recorded on a honeypot around 2026-10-24, and Dream Security later reported 25 servers rooted by chaining PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia kernel flaw.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Amazon Threat Intelligence via BleepingComputer: attempts (non-functional exploits, against a honeypot) from 2026-10-17, four days before patches; first confirmed successful in-the-wild RCE was Adel Karimi's honeypot report dated 2026-10-24 (BleepingComputer 2026-10-26)
